column1: # AQL Language Specification: the aql:parselang module + the core `parse` word
# `parse <kind> <opts?> <source>` is the sibling of `mini`: it expands at the
# call site to the STANDARD parser call `ParseLang.parse_<kind> <source> <opts>
# end`. Unlike `mini`, the `source` is the REQUIRED LAST surface arg (a String
# or a {src:…} Source map) and `opts` is the optional MIDDLE one — disambiguated
# by arity. A parser returns Any (an AST, a transduction, …). `ParseLang.register`
# installs AQL fns as parsers; `ParseLang.kinds` lists them; `ParseLang.source`
# resolves a source value to its String. These rows register a small `calc`
# parser whose AST is the token list `[left op right]` (built by StringUtil.split
# on the resolved source). A {file:…} source is deferred in v1.
# §1  parse — an AQL-registered parser returning a tokenization
import "aql:parselang"  import "aql:string-util"  ParseLang.register calc (fn [[source:Any opts:Map] [List] [StringUtil.split ' ' (ParseLang.source source)]]) end  (parse calc 'x + y') get 1
column3: the parsed operator token

column1: # §9  aontu — the built-in aontu parser, the upstream Go port of
#     github.com/rjrodger/aontu (the repo's go/ module), a CUE-inspired
#     unification config dialect. It parses, unifies and generates the source
#     to a Node of Maps and Lists: top-level `k:v` entries and the colon-chain
#     `a:b:c:1` build maps, `[…]` builds lists, duplicate keys and `&`
#     scalars, an absolute `$.a` reference resolves from the root and a relative
#     `.k` reference resolves a sibling key at the current map level.

column3: top-level key/value entries build a Map
the colon-chain a:b:c:1 nests Maps
a [list] builds a List; elements may be comma- or space-separated
duplicate keys deep-merge their Maps (unification)
a kind word unifies with a matching scalar to yield the scalar
an absolute $ reference resolves from the document root
a reference indexes into a list
parse is pure sugar — the desugared standard call is equivalent

column1: # §10  a ParseLang VALUE as the parser — `parse <fn> <opts?> <source>`. The
#      first operand may BE the parser: a Function (or a word bound to one)
#      whose every signature starts with the standard [source opts] prefix —
#      the same contract ParseLang.register enforces. The call expands to the
#      direct fn call `<fn> <source> <opts> end` with no kind lookup, so a
#      parser works without being registered under a kind name. A registered
#      kind wins a name collision. (A parser COMPUTED by a runtime call —
#      `parse (mk) 'x'` — works interpreted but the compiled path currently
#      refuses its operand provenance, so that form is pinned in
#      lang/go/test/parselang_host_test.go rather than as a row here.)
